ALASKA
IT'SOD
The spectacular beauty, unique history and
unusual culture of our great 49th state have
inspired artists, poets, and songwriters of
many eras. In this authentic album, the
exciting voices of the Harry Simeone Chorale
sing out for Alaska with songs composed by
Elizabeth Firestone Willis especially for the
show, "It's Alaska," a Broadway-type musical
production. "Let's Go To Alaska" was the
official theme song for Alaska's Centennial
Exposition. Elizabeth composed the music and
the lyrics were written by Larry Beck,
well-known northland poet and student of
Robert Service. "It's Alaska" took its audi-
ences on a simulated tour of Alaska through
song, dance and film. "Stops" were made
along the "tour" in such places as Nome.
Sitka, Fairbanks and Anchorage. And while
"in" Anchorage the audience watched the
famous Fur Rendezvous Bob Sled Races where
the winner sang "That's What Happy is For."
Also, "near" Anchorage, the audience visited
Mt. Alyeska Ski Resort and heard the
romantic strains of "Under the Starlight,"
and later enjoyed a "Swingin' Sleigh Ride."
Everything that is Alaskan, from the raucous
Golden Nugget Saloon to the historical Otto
Von Kotzebue, is here. It's Alaska!
HARRY SIMEONE
In arranging and conducting the music for
this album, Simeone has captured the true
excitement of Alaska. His artistrv is the
result of many successful years as composer,
author, conductor and arranger. Simeone
and the Harry Simeone Chorale, are perhaps
best known for "The Little Drummer Boy,"
highly popular Christmastime song. Harry
began his career as a CBS staff arranger
after graduation from the Juilliard School of
Music. From 1939 to 1945, he was arranger
for Fred Waring and then moved to Para-
mount Pictures in Hollywood. There, he
worked with Victor Young on "The Affairs of
Susan" and the Crosby-Hope "Road" pictures.
Simeone has been choral director for the
Firestone Hour and he has arranged for
many important TV shows. Simeone's hit,
"The Little Drummer Boy," comes from his
first album for 20th-Fox Records, "Sing Me
Now of Christmas." Other Simeone songs
and instrumentals include: "The Magic of
Love." "Three Mother Geese." "Button.
Button, Let's Push the Button," "Nursery
Rhyme Suite," and "Rumanian Rhapsody."
Several million copies of Simeone's original
compositions and arrangements have been
sold over the past few years and currently
his Harry Simeone Chorale albums are being
enjoyed in homes throughout the nation.
ELIZABETH FIRESTONE WILLIS
Elizabeth Firestone Willis is an accomplished
pianist and composer. She has performed
in concert halls in the United States and
Europe, and has composed popular and
classical music. including songs and cenrec
for motion pictures made in this country
and Snain
Mrs. Willis has performed on nationwide
radio and television, including a broadcast
featuring her "Rhapsodie Moderne." Among
her New York concert appearances was one at
Carnegie Hall where she was on a program
with Christopher Lynch, the noted Irish
tenor, in his American debut. This was also
the occasion for the premiere of "Fantasy."
"Concertino," a "small concerto," she wrote
for piano and orchestra, was performed by
Mrs. Willis originally on the National Broad-
casting System (NBC) network, and received
substantial critical acclaim throughout the
country. She later introduced this composi-
tion to British audiences in a concert at Royal
Albert Hall where she performed with
the London Symphony.
In the field of motion pictures, she wrote the
musical score for Robert Montgomer's
"Once More, My Darling" in Hollywood. And
in Spain, European musicians first became
familiar with her work when she wrote the
score for "That Man From Tangier" which
was filmed there.
Listed in "Who's Who of American Women,"
Mrs. Willis is a member of the Board of
Trustees of the National Symphony Orchestra
in Washington, D.C., and a member of the
National Council of the Metropolitan Opera
Association. In private life she is the wife of
Charles F. Willis, Jr., president of
Alaska Airlines,
